# Inkwell

> Last updated: 2026-09-05
> Full reference: https://inkwell.world/llms-full.txt

> Inkwell is a calm, distraction-free writing home for novelists. It combines a
> focused editor with connected world-building tools (characters, lore, and
> story elements), so writers can start a project in seconds and stay
> organized as their story grows. Inkwell's positioning is "the best place to
> actually finish your novel."

Inkwell works in any modern browser, syncs across devices, and supports
offline writing. Documents export as Markdown, plain text, PDF, DOCX, or EPUB.
There is a free plan (Inkling) and a paid plan (Storyteller, $9/month) with a
higher-tier plan (Worldbuilder) coming soon.

Inkwell does not brand its features as "AI." Story intelligence features
(summarization, brainstorming, keeping the story connected) are described by
their outcome, not by the underlying technology.

The Compass is Inkwell's set of writing analysis tools, all drawn from a
writer's own manuscript: Synopsis (a short factual recap of any document),
Heartbeat (a dramatic-tension curve across the whole work), Ask (plain-language
questions answered from the prose, with a link back to the passage), and the
Atlas (a relationship map built from the writing, coming soon on Worldbuilder).

## Key pages

- [Home](https://inkwell.world/): overview, features, and how to start writing in seconds.
- [The Compass](https://inkwell.world/compass): writing analysis tools (Synopsis, Heartbeat, Ask, and the Atlas) drawn from your own manuscript.
- [Start Your Story Challenge](https://inkwell.world/start-your-story): write 10,000 words across 5 writing days in your first two weeks and earn a free month of Storyteller.
- [Pricing](https://inkwell.world/pricing): plans and what's included in each.
- [Learn](https://inkwell.world/learn): craft guides for novelists, written for writers using any tool.

## Craft guides

Practical, tool-agnostic guides for novelists, published under /learn. They are
written to be useful to any writer, whether or not they use Inkwell.

- [How to outline a novel](https://inkwell.world/learn/how-to-outline-a-novel): six outlining methods compared (beat sheet, snowflake, index cards, chapter grid, reverse outline, guardrails), how much to plan before drafting, and what to do when the draft diverges from the outline.
- [How to write a story bible](https://inkwell.world/learn/how-to-write-a-story-bible): what a story bible is (a reference document of what is true, as distinct from an outline of what happens), when to start one, the six sections that matter, and a copyable template.
- [How to build a character profile](https://inkwell.world/learn/how-to-build-a-character-profile): why long character questionnaires produce flat characters, the fields that change your prose (want, need, the lie, voice, behaviour under pressure), and a copyable template.
- [How to plan a book series](https://inkwell.world/learn/how-to-plan-a-book-series): choosing a series shape, balancing the series arc against each book's own arc, seeding book one, ending each book, and keeping continuity across books.

## Full reference

A longer document with complete plan contents, feature descriptions, the
comparison matrix, and the questions writers ask is at
https://inkwell.world/llms-full.txt

## Getting started

Writers can start using Inkwell immediately at https://app.inkwell.world/auth,
no download or installation required.
